gloss: the pathos of things; mono no aware

definitions.gloss: the pathos of things; sensitivity to transience
definitions.explanation: A classical aesthetic ideal: the quiet, moving sadness felt on sensing that beautiful things pass. Associated above all with Heian literature and with the reading of {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}.

examples.japanese: {物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: I feel the pathos of things.

examples.japanese: {散|ち}る{桜|さくら}に{物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れを{覚|おぼ}えた。
examples.english: The falling cherry blossoms stirred a sense of the pathos of things in me.

examples.japanese: {本居宣長|もとおりのりなが}は、{源氏物語|げんじものがたり}の{本質|ほんしつ}は{物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れにあると{説|と}いた。
examples.english: Motoori Norinaga argued that the essence of The Tale of Genji lies in mono no aware.

notes:
Often written without kanji as もののあはれ in classical texts and as もののあわれ in modern ones. The Edo scholar {本居宣長|もとおりのりなが} made the phrase the centre of his reading of Heian literature, and it has been treated as a defining Japanese aesthetic ever since.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れを{感|かん}じる: to feel the pathos of things
- {物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れを{知|し}る: to be sensitive to the pathos of things
- {物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れの{美|び}: the beauty of transience

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {無常|むじょう}: impermanence — the Buddhist doctrine behind the feeling, not the feeling itself
- {侘|わ}び{寂|さび}: wabi-sabi — beauty in simplicity and age, a related but distinct ideal
- {切|せつ}ない: bittersweet, aching — the everyday adjective for a comparable emotion
